originality.rationale: The defining Fromage source gives the update and purpose of its prefactor but not the sharp SPD condition-number theorem. Earlier proportional-update work already covers qualitative fixed-rate failure on shifted scalar objectives, so novelty is restricted to the exact prefactor-induced centered law, its sharp LARS comparison, and the exact Fromage rotation boundary.
residual_risks: A mathematically equivalent sharp centered formula may exist in older normalized-gradient or numerical linear-algebra literature under terminology unrelated to Fromage.
Qualitative fixed-step nonconvergence on shifted one-dimensional proportional updates is prior art; only the exact Fromage-prefactor rotation refinement is treated as part of the final claim.
The centered one-step worst-case witness need not remain an equality trajectory at every iteration, so the theorem does not claim a sharp asymptotic lower bound.

value.rationale: Fromage was distinguished from LARS by exactly the prefactor analyzed here. The result shows that this factor removes the centered proportional-update stability ceiling and changes the sharp worst-case one-step conditioning dependence from \(1-\Theta(\kappa^{-1})\) to \(1-\Theta(\kappa^{-1/2})\). The shifted rotation boundary explains the price of that behavior: the guarantee is tied to origin-relative geometry and cannot be transferred to translated objectives.
